title: Doing scientific investigation
competency: Describe the steps of a scientific investigation and carry out a fair test.

keywords.def: The process by which scientists approach their work: question, research, hypothesis, test, conclude, communicate.
A tentative explanation for a set of observations, with predictions that can be tested.
An experiment where you change only one factor and keep all the others the same.

en.text: Scientists work in steps: ask a question, do background research, make a hypothesis, test it with an experiment, analyse the results and draw a conclusion, then communicate. If the hypothesis is wrong, make a new one and test again.

am.text: ሳይንቲስቶች በደረጃ ይሰራሉ፤ ጥያቄ ይጠይቃሉ፣ ቅድመ ጥናት ያደርጋሉ፣ መላምት ያቀርባሉ፣ በሙከራ ይፈትናሉ፣ ውጤቱን ይተነትናሉ፣ ያሳውቃሉ።

screens.title: Taller teff
screens.ask: You notice that teff in one field grows taller than in another. What should a scientist do first?
opts: Ask a question she can test
screens.after: Start with a question, like "Does fertiliser make teff grow taller?" Observations lead to questions.
screens.best: Ask a question she can test

screens.title: Scientific investigation
paras: Science is learning about the world through observation and inquiry.
Scientists form and test hypotheses, gather and analyse data, then report.
This process is called the scientific investigation or scientific method.

screens.title: Figure 1.9: steps in the scientific method
items: Observations lead to a question that can be measured and answered by experiment.
Find information online, in a library or from earlier studies.
A tentative, logical explanation with predictions you can test.
Do an experiment that someone else can repeat. Keep conditions the same.
Do the results support the hypothesis? If not, make a new one.
Share your methods and results so others can check them.

screens.title: Key words
defs: The process by which scientists approach their work: question, research, hypothesis, test, conclude, communicate.
A tentative explanation for a set of observations, with predictions that can be tested.

screens.title: The scientific method on a teff farm
steps: 1 Ask: does fertiliser make teff grow taller?
2 Research: talk to the local agricultural extension worker. Read about fertiliser.
3 Hypothesis: teff with fertiliser grows taller than teff without it.
4 Test: use two plots with the same seed, soil, water and sowing day. Add fertiliser to one plot only.
5 Analyse: measure the plants in both plots each week. Compare the heights. Do they support the hypothesis?
6 Communicate: share the results with farmers and your class.

screens.text: Scientific method: put the six steps in order.
items: Analyse the results and draw a conclusion
screens.why:
1 Ask a question about what you observe.
2 Do background research.
3 Make a hypothesis you can test.
4 Test it with an experiment.
5 Analyse the results and draw a conclusion.
6 Communicate the results.
screens.clue: It starts with a question and ends with sharing.

screens.text: Key words: what is a hypothesis?
opts: A tentative explanation that can be tested
screens.ans: A tentative explanation that can be tested
screens.why:
A hypothesis is a tentative (not yet proven) explanation.
It makes predictions you can test.
An experiment then supports it, or not.
A proven law is not a hypothesis: it has already been tested many times.

screens.text: Scientific method: your results do not support your hypothesis. What do you do?
opts: Make a new hypothesis and test again
Report that the hypothesis was right
screens.ans: Make a new hypothesis and test again
screens.why:
Results that do not fit are still useful.
They tell you the hypothesis may be wrong.
Make a new hypothesis.
Go back to step 3 and test it with a new experiment.
Never change the results.
screens.clue: Look at the "Try again" arrow in Figure 1.9.

screens.text: Communicating results, true or false: it lets other scientists check your methods and results.
screens.why:
Step 6 is to communicate your results.
You share your methods and results in writing or orally.
Others can repeat your experiment to check it.
So the statement is true.

screens.text: Checking results: two schools test the same hypothesis and get different results. What does this mean?
opts: The hypothesis may not be supported; check the methods
screens.ans: The hypothesis may not be supported; check the methods
screens.why:
Science needs results that others can repeat.
Different results mean the question is not settled.
The hypothesis may not be supported.
Scientists compare methods and look for mistakes.
No result wins just because it came first.
screens.clue: What does step 6 say about other researchers?

en.text: In a fair test you change only one factor and keep all others the same, and you repeat the experiment. In Example 1.9 a burning candle covered with a gas jar goes out, which shows that air (oxygen) is needed for burning.

am.text: በፍትሐዊ ሙከራ አንድ ነገር ብቻ ትቀይራለህ፣ ሌሎቹን ሁሉ ታቆያለህ። ሻማ በብርጭቆ ሲሸፈን ይጠፋል፤ ይህ ለማቃጠል አየር እንደሚያስፈልግ ያሳያል።

screens.title: Candle under a jar
screens.ask: A lit candle is covered with an upside-down glass jar. What happens?
opts: It goes out after a short time
screens.after: It goes out. The flame uses up the oxygen in the jar.
screens.best: It goes out after a short time

screens.title: Example 1.9: is air needed for burning?
steps: Question: is air necessary for burning?
Research: books say air is necessary for burning.
Hypothesis: air is needed for burning.
Test: light a candle. It keeps burning in fresh air. Cover it with an inverted gas jar: soon it goes out.
Conclusion: the candle used the oxygen in the jar. Air is necessary for burning.
Communicate: report the result in writing or orally.

screens.title: Keep it fair
paras: If you change any factor, keep all the others the same.
Repeat it a few more times to make sure the results are accurate.

screens.title: Key words
defs: An experiment where you change only one factor and keep all the others the same.

screens.text: Fair test (Activity 1.7 a): you test if sunlight affects bean growth. What must you keep the same in both pots?
screens.why:
The factor you test is sunlight.
So only sunlight is different between the pots.
Soil, water and pot size must stay the same.
Then any difference comes from sunlight.
screens.clue: Which one factor are you testing?

screens.title: Change or keep the same?
screens.text: Fair test (Activity 1.7 a): you test if sunlight affects bean growth. Sort each factor.
items: This is the one factor you test.
A bigger pot could also change growth.
screens.why:
You are testing sunlight, so only sunlight changes.
Soil, water, pot size and the kind of bean all affect growth.
So they must stay the same in both pots.
Then any difference comes from sunlight.
screens.clue: Which one factor is the experiment about?

screens.text: Candle experiment: why does the candle go out under the jar?
opts: The oxygen in the jar gets used up
screens.ans: The oxygen in the jar gets used up
screens.why:
A flame needs oxygen from the air.
The jar traps only a little air.
The candle uses up the oxygen in it.
When too little oxygen is left, the flame goes out.
The wax has not run out: the candle relights in fresh air.
screens.clue: What does a flame need from the air?

screens.text: Fair test: Lemlem tests beans. Pot A is in the sun with water; pot B is in the dark with no water. Pot A grows better. What is wrong?
opts: She changed two factors, so it is not a fair test
She should use three pots of sand
screens.ans: She changed two factors, so it is not a fair test
screens.why:
Count the differences between the pots.
Light is different, and water is different: two factors.
Pot A may grow better because of light, or water, or both.
Lemlem cannot tell which.
A fair test changes only one factor.
screens.clue: How many things were different between the pots?

screens.text: Fair test, true or false: after an experiment, you should repeat it a few times.
screens.why:
One result could be a mistake or chance.
Repeating the experiment checks it.
If the results agree, you can trust them more.
The book says repeat it a few times. So it is true.

screens.text: Fair test: Abel wants to know if salt makes water boil faster. Which plan is a fair test?
opts: Two same pots, same amount of water, same stove; add salt to one only
One pot with salt on a big stove, one without on a small stove
Boil salty water once and stop
screens.ans: Two same pots, same amount of water, same stove; add salt to one only
screens.why:
The factor to test is salt.
In the first plan only the salt changes.
Pot, amount of water and stove stay the same.
So any difference in boiling time comes from the salt.
The second plan also changes the stove, so it is not fair.

items.text: Activity 1.7 a, predict: a bean plant kept in the dark for two weeks will most likely be
opts: greener than one in the sun
items.why:
Green plants need light to make their food.
In the dark the plant cannot make enough food.
It grows thin and tall, looking for light.
Its leaves turn pale.
So it is thin, pale and weak.
items.clue: What do plants need light for?

items.text: Activity 1.7 b, predict: wire is coiled around a nail and joined to a battery. The nail
opts: picks up pins: it acts like a magnet
items.ans: picks up pins: it acts like a magnet
items.why:
The battery sends a current through the coil.
A current in a coil makes a magnetic field.
The iron nail inside becomes a magnet: an electromagnet.
So it picks up pins.
items.clue: What does current in a coil do?

items.text: Activity 1.7 c, food test: a leaf from the sun turns blue-black with iodine. This shows the leaf stores
items.why:
Iodine is a test for starch.
With starch, brown iodine turns blue-black.
A leaf in the sun makes sugar by photosynthesis.
It stores the extra sugar as starch.
So the leaf stores starch.

items.text: Exercise 1.13, scientific method: put its components in order.
items.why:
1 Ask a question about what you observe.
2 Do background research.
3 Make a hypothesis you can test.
4 Test it with an experiment.
5 Analyse the results and draw a conclusion.
6 Communicate the results.

test.text: Scientific method: the first step is
test.why:
Science begins with an observation.
The observation leads to a question.
So the first step is to ask questions.
Research, hypothesis and testing come after.

test.text: Scientific method: the last step is
test.why:
After testing, you analyse and conclude.
Then you share your work with others.
So the last step is to communicate results.
Asking questions is the first step.

test.text: Hypothesis: a good hypothesis must be
opts: based on scientific knowledge and logical
test.ans: based on scientific knowledge and logical
test.why:
A hypothesis is a tentative explanation.
It should be logical and based on scientific knowledge.
It does not have to be correct: a test may reject it.
It is not a measurement or a final report.

test.text: Fair test: in a fair test you change
test.why:
You want to know what one factor does.
So change only that factor.
Keep all the others the same.
If you change two, you cannot tell which caused the result.

test.text: Candle experiment: a candle under a jar goes out. This shows that burning needs
test.why:
In fresh air the candle keeps burning.
Under the jar it soon goes out.
The only change: the oxygen in the air runs low.
So burning needs air (oxygen).
